newsitem.title: FRANCE: Carlos the Jackal issues anti-German "Nazi" jibe.
newsitem.headline: Carlos the Jackal issues anti-German "Nazi" jibe.

text.p: Guerrilla mastermind "Carlos the Jackal" branded German judges on Friday as "the unworthy heirs of Nazi justice" in a message sent out of his Paris jail.

In a statement made available to Reuters by his lawyer, Carlos explained why he refused to answer questions this week on the role played by Hans-Joachim Klein, a German accomplice in the kidnapping of 11 OPEC oil ministers in Vienna in 1975.
Venezuelan-born Carlos, whose real name is Illich Ramirez Sanchez, was arrested in August 1994 and is being held in La Sante prison, in Paris.

Frankfurt state attorney Volker Rath, with Guido Schneider and Michaela Ragg of the German police, met Carlos in the office of France's top anti-terrorism investigating magistrate Jean-Louis Bruguiere on Wednesday.

Carlos hit out at German authorities for sentencing 43-year-old Palestinian mother Souhaila Andrawes to 12 years in jail this month for her role in the hijacking of a Lufthansa airliner to Mogadishu, capital of Somalia, in October 1977.
Andrawes is the only survivor of four Palestinians who hijacked the plane to back demands by German Red Army Faction (RAF) guerrillas.
The hijackers wanted to help free 11 RAF members from jail. When their demands were not met, they shot the pilot in the head.
A five-day ordeal for the remaining 86 hostages ended when West German commandos stormed the aircraft in Mogadishu. They killed all the hijackers except Andrawes.

Andrawes was convicted in Somalia for the hijacking and sentenced to 20 years in jail but was released after a year and went home to Beirut. She moved to Norway in 1991 and was extradited to Germany four years later.
Carlos said West German authorities and Somalia's then-president Mohamed Siad Barre had agreed that any hijackers who survived a commando raid to free the hostages would be tried in Somalia.

"After she was sentenced by a Somali court, Comrade Souhaila purged part of her sentence and was freed for medical reasons which were morally and legally justified: she had to be operated on several times in Prague so as to be able to walk," Carlos said in the statement, part of which was the text of his deposition before the German investigators.

"In putting (Andrawes) on trial a second time, West Germany violated in scandalous fashion a fundamental principle of justice" under which suspects cannot be tried twice for the same offence, he said.
Carlos concluded: "The German judges are the unworthy heirs of Nazi justice!" He signed his statement: "Illich Ramirez Sanchez".
The OPEC kidnapping was the most audacious of a series of attacks by Carlos. France says he killed 83 people in the 1970s and 1980s in a series of attacks in Europe and the Middle East.
